item.title: Our verdict on Lawson earning a 2027 F1 extension
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue to race for Racing Bulls in 2027, with Red Bull electing against what would have been a huge Formula 1 driver sacking. Here's what our team makes of the move to keep Lawson and Lindblad and not promote Formula 2 title contender Nikola Tsolov into a race seat. An existential question has been answered Very few driver decisions have felt as right as Lawson getting a fresh contract with Racing Bulls.He has been superb this year. Yes, there are still some rough edges to smooth out, but he has been fast throughout, consistently strong, delivering technical input that his engineers have loved, and brilliantly able to shut out all the noise regarding the doubts over his future.But there is a wider significance to Lawson getting a stay, and it's one I mentioned in Monday's From the Paddock newsletter. The Lawson decision was almost existential for Racing Bulls in telling us what that team is really about.Sign up to our newsletter to be in with a chance of winning a signed Valtteri Bottas Cadillac F1 cap. Is it an outfit that, under Alan Permane, can stand on its own two feet, take its own decisions and plot a path that is only focused on making itself better?Or is it simply a puppet for sister squad Red Bull, a testing ground and training school for its future drivers, even if that means some short-term pain in rushing rookies through?After the season Lawson has had, it would have made no sense for Racing Bulls to drop him and throw away all the good momentum it has built up. So keeping him for now gives us the answer about what Racing Bulls is about.Tsolov has a bright future in F1, but time is on his side to make that step up.The best decision for all involvedPretty sure this is the best decision for Racing Bulls and in the future for Red Bull.Both Lawson and Lindblad - a rookie, let's not forget - have shown that they can bring home the results when everything goes as planned over a race weekend.Both are capable of being a replacement for Isack Hadjar or Max Verstappen if either of them slip on a banana skin. Red Bull knows what Lawson can bring to them if required, so he is a good measure of what Lindblad could potentially bring too.Having Tsolov in the background and doing a few FP1 sessions will prepare him for an introduction in 2028.As far as I'm concerned, it's the correct decision for all involved. Credibility for Racing Bulls If Racing Bulls is to be at all seen as an F1 team in its own right, with its own ambitions and dreams and what have you, rather than a pure Red Bull talent farm, then yeah, Lawson pretty much had to be kept on.Tsolov may end up faster down the line. For all we know, he may be faster already. But the kind of efficient scoring that Lawson has provided this year a rookie cannot match - I would say that's a rule in F1. So Tsolov-for-Lawson would be nakedly sacrificing Racing Bulls's present for the senior Red Bull team's future, and every decision like that makes it less and less palatable for Red Bull to own two teams in F1.Only if Racing Bulls has its own aspirations can it be allowed to continue, and a new deal for Lawson buys some credibility in my eyes.Marko would have dropped Lawson long agoAt the height of his powers, Helmut Marko would have ditched Lawson ages ago.Lawson had his shot at the top team, didn't make it, and will likely not be given that chance again.Now Marko's no longer in charge, and this is the biggest indicator yet that Racing Bulls is not Toro Rosso; developing young drivers is no longer the only, or primary, end goal for this team.You can't blame Red Bull. Instead of a team that cost and lost money to run like Toro Rosso, Racing Bulls is now a multi-billion dollar entity. Constructors' championship finishing position is not the only definition of value in an F1 business anymore.Taking risks with a team built with the acceptance of losing money is one thing. Taking risks with a team worth billions is another.None of this is to criticise the decision it has made, as Lawson is a worthy F1 driver. It's just to point out yet more evidence that Racing Bulls is acting and being run like its own team.Lawson would be wise to find an exit route Lawson is in a fantastic position now and has been one of the star drivers of the season, but he should already be thinking about exit routes for 2028.Tsolov is going to be waiting in the wings next year, and there's no reason why Racing Bulls might be faced with the exact same 'three into two' dilemma for 2028. This time Lawson was the overwhelmingly logical pick, next time he might not be and, given Red Bull leaves those decisions until late in the season, he doesn't want to suddenly be left without a seat for 2028.So he'd be wise to try to follow the Pierre Gasly and Carlos Sainz playbook of finding another driver Red Bull decides it's done with you. Adds to an excellent redemption arc I've got a lot of time for this career redemption arc.Lawson at the Red Bull senior team always felt like an uncomfortable fit to me, right from when it was announced. I certainly hadn't seen anything to suggest he would solve the team's second-driver problem.Red Bull's bungling of what followed didn't help, but that ill-fated, two-race spell could've marked the beginning of the end of Lawson's F1 career.Instead, what's followed has revealed plenty about his mental resolve - because he's had to process a lot these past 20 months yet has been absolutely unflappable. Driving for the top teams is what every driver craves, but it doesn't have to be the be-all and end-all and, if you don't make it, it doesn't automatically consign you to career collapse.Lawson's proved emphatically this year that he deserves a place in F1. This contract extension was therefore the only acceptable outcome.

item.title: Cavaliers 115, Knicks 107: “Credit them, but…”
item.author: Moritz Wollert
item.content:encoded: As sports fans, our teams give us plenty to think about and then some. They give us stuff to bicker, to complain, to ramble about. We follow their every move meticulously, we break down the potential of prospective grocery baggers and hail them as the next coming. We love to read or listen to others doing the same, even or especially if we do not agree with their viewpoints. Lucky fanatics get something to cheer about every once in a while – consider that box checked by our beloved New York Knickerbockers lately.Understandably, that focus on one team, that love for one franchise can lead to kind of a narrow view on things at times. Nothing wrong with that; fandom doesn’t have to be rational, it doesn’t have to explain itself. And it does not necessarily have to involve the other team’s perspective or, frankly, the other team at all. At times though, that group in the different colored jerseys is the biggest answer to the question you have regarding your own squad’s performance.Last night felt exactly like that kind of game where the Knicks did a lot of stuff well, but in the end the Cleveland Cavaliers just did most of it a little bit better. And when the Knicks didn’t do something as well, it was also the Cavaliers who had a hand in that. From the opening tip, it was obvious that the Cavs wanted this one – analytically and this time around actually in reality, too. They remembered last Saturday when New York rained on their Rocket Arena parade on the second night of a back-to-back; they surely remembered the last time they visited Madison Square Garden. And it looked like they were tired of the narrative that had them as the soft wannabes that can’t keep up when the orange and blue drivers push the pedals to the metal.Cavaliers put an end to Knicks’ winning streakDonovan Mitchell lived in the lane for most of the night; every high slip screen was an automatic downhill and kick opportunity for the team from Ohio, and their old and new length bothered the smaller Knicks for long stretches of the game. Peyton Watson might not be able to hit the water from the Verrazzano Bridge right now, but he sure can impact a game defensively. A lot of the Ohioans were feeling good about themselves; Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas gave youthful, quality energy off the bench. And then, of course, there was James Harden. That guy who is a poster child for a lot of ugly wrongs in the modern game, the one who has been awful all year long so far but decided to show up for this one and give his team a vintage performance in the very building he crapped the postseason bed in just half a year ago.So even if, at least in Harden’s case, it’s hard to stomach, let’s follow Knicks Fan in Jerusalem’s proposal from the Postgame Thread that gave this text its headline. Let’s credit the Cavaliers for a game well played, for shots hit, for storms weathered. But as the headline and our friend in Israel suggested, there’s another side to the story, a “but”. Tipping our collective cap to the Cavs sure doesn’t mean the Knicks can’t do a lot of things better in the future. Jalen Brunson had a good scoring game yet failed to deliver any rhythm to the offense. Too many times the ball just stuck on the perimeter (a particular problem for OG Anunoby right now), and there wasn’t nearly enough off-ball movement to stretch a much bigger defense that wants you to finish over their size.That size played quite a role in yesterday’s contest, be it on the boards or in the passing lanes. Unfortunately, the Knicks won’t get any taller, that’s for sure. Mike Brown tried to counter Cleveland’s length by going to Mohamed Diawara early in the absence of Jordan Clarkson. Mo had a nice drive and, in theory, could be a solution for physical matchup problems like this one, but clearly isn’t there yet. The young Frenchman seems unsure about himself, plays hesitantly, and is missing the wide-open shots he knocked down in his sleep last season. His defense mostly looks good but not good enough to warrant a bigger role yet.So, what’s happening with Mikal Bridges?Aside from plenty of mental lapses, missing open shots was a problem for Josh Hart last night as well, but we excuse the veteran as he clearly had to shake off some rust after his injury break. That doesn’t change the fact that his lack of consistent outside shooting can become an issue at times, especially against good teams that willingly put roaming defenders on him. Normally, he adds so many other intangibles that you can live with it in the bigger picture more often than not. In Mikal Bridges’ case, though, well, what’s there right now? Hounding defense? Don’t see it consistently. A presence off the ball? Nope. Secondary scoring? Corner threes? Emotion? Desperation? Anything?Bridges once again played an uneventful, meager 17 minutes in this one. Plenty of the other guards – Deuce McBride, Landry Shamet, and Tyler Kolek – currently do everything Bridges is paid for and actually a bit more. The longer this situation drags on, the louder Mike Brown will hear the question: When will you make a change to the starting lineup? It’s easy to understand why he’s reluctant; he sure doesn’t want to create an internal problem by benching someone who did his part in winning a championship last year. But what if the problem is creating itself? There’s a tipping point to everything.For the Knicks, this game won’t be one, and it shouldn’t be. There might be some stuff to think about, though, going forward. Just like we want to have it as fans.

item.title: Denmark announced as host of 2027 UEC Road European Championships
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: It's the first time the nation has hosted a major road championship since the 2017 European Championships, also held in Herning, when Alexander Kristoff and Marianne Vos raced to glory in the road races while Victor Campenaerts and Ellen van Dijk won the time trials.Previously, the Road World Championships were held in Copenhagen, Denmark, in 2011, while the Road Worlds will head back to the nation in 2029.Previous major championships held in Denmark have ended with mass sprint finishes, and the 2027 European Championships are also expected to favour sprinters after hilly editions in Slovenia and France in the last two years.The 2027 UEC Road European Championships will run between September 28 and October 3, and while the exact dates of each event are not yet known, that creates a clash with La Vuelta Femenina, which begins on October 3. "We are thrilled to be returning to Denmark after ten years. In 2017, this country hosted the second edition of the Road European Championships open to the Elite category, believing from the outset in a project that was then in its infancy," said UEC president Enrico Della Casa."Today, we are returning with an event that has grown considerably and has become a world-class occasion, capable of attracting the attention of the media and cycling enthusiasts from all over the world."Hosting of the European Championships is now set for the next three years, with trips to Denmark, the North Brabant region of the Netherlands, and Abruzzo in Italy on the way."With Denmark in 2027, the Netherlands in 2028 and Italy, specifically the Abruzzo region, in 2029, the next three years promise to be highly prestigious for the UEC Road European Championships. These three countries, each with a deeply rooted cycling culture, demonstrate the appeal our event has gained and allow us to look to the future with great ambition," said Della Casa."I would like to thank the cities of Herning and Silkeborg, Sport Event Denmark, the Danish government and the Danish Cycling Federation and its President, Morten Anderson, for the trust, enthusiasm and commitment they have shown."Ten years ago, Denmark helped to write an important chapter in the history of our European Championships, and I am convinced that in 2027, together we will write another equally memorable one."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Red Bull's Lawson decision is a clean break from its Marko era
item.author: Edd Straw
item.content:encoded: Lawson’s seat in Red Bull’s second team has been at very real risk in recent rounds, with Formula 2 race winner Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings and Red Bull needing to decide which two of Lawson, Tsolov and Arvid Lindblad race for Racing Bulls next year. But had Lawson lost out - with zero options elsewhere on the grid to race in 2027 - it would have been an unprecedented move.In the past 10 seasons of F1, there have only been two comparable cases of a driver doing as well as Lawson is currently doing, getting dropped and then not having an alternative seat for the following season.Only Sergio Perez - who was eighth in the 2024 championship - and Alex Albon - who was seventh in the 2020 championship - have been higher placed than Lawson is right now (ninth) and yet found themselves without a drive the year after.Both, of course, met that fate thanks to Red Bull, but the big difference is both Perez and Albon were driving for Red Bull Racing - and getting absolutely destroyed by Max Verstappen in the process.Lawson is in a completely different situation here, in that he’s the highest-placed of all midfield drivers in the 2026 world championship and comfortably ahead of his rookie team-mate Lindblad.The main threat to Lawson’s position comes from F2 title contender Tsolov. The Bulgarian has won six races in his rookie F2 season and sits only seven points behind 2027 Haas F1 driver and Ferrari junior Rafael Camara - who made his F1 debut in place of Esteban Ocon in Brazil.Tsolov has made a strong case for promotion, not only because of those F2 results but also because of how well he did subbing for Lawson in a mandated rookie FP1 outing in Mexico, where Tsolov lapped within two tenths of Lindblad and generally looked very at ease with the whole business of being in F1.On top of Tsolov’s impressive showing in Mexico, Lawson later had a run-in with Red Bull’s kingpin driver Verstappen during FP2 - which earned Lawson a strong rebuke from the four-time champion, in which Verstappen alluded to Lawson’s 2027 deal uncertainty.The Race understands the recent triple-header has basically been the crunch moment for Red Bull and Racing Bulls to do their final analysis on who should drive next year - so Lawson been under pressure during this period and at genuine risk of losing his seat.Which perhaps explains Verstappen’s pointed remark in the wake of their collision in Mexico, “It’s just not very smart behaviour when you’re in his position to pick a fight with me.”But the way Lawson rebounded from that low point, recovering from a technical exclusion in qualifying and a pitlane start to finish seventh that weekend, in his familiar position as the leading midfield runner, showed true grit.Add that to the way Lawson excelled in the wet in Brazil - fifth in qualifying and seventh in the race - and it’s difficult for anyone inside the Red Bull system to make the case he should definitely be dropped.It has only been Lawson at real risk - because Lindblad has done an excellent job alongside him as a rookie and contributed a meaningful 35% of the points that leave Racing Bulls almost certain to finish fifth in the constructors’ championship - the highest place in the team’s history.Lawson’s job within that team is essentially to give Red Bull a benchmark of performance to measure Lindblad against. There’s no realistic possibility of Lawson becoming a contender for a Red Bull Racing seat again, in the way there might still be for Lindblad or, eventually, Tsolov.The trouble is that Lawson has done such an excellent job in his role this season - and has even taken a further step as a driver since subbing for Isack Hadjar at Red Bull for three races - that he made himself impossible to drop even though his presence no longer really fits the 'Red Bull conveyor belt' function Racing Bulls is supposed to have.On Friday in Brazil, Racing Bulls team boss Alan Permane said Racing Bulls is trying to “apply a little bit of science” to the situation, a clear rebuke of the days when Helmut Marko would hire and fire junior drivers seemingly almost on a whim. “Red Bull's had a very successful young driver programme, and if I want to be... and I don't want to be critical of it, but I think if you guys are critical of it, maybe sometimes the drivers haven't been able to have enough time to settle, or maybe some snap decisions have been made,” Permane said.Lawson’s average qualifying advantage over Lindblad is only seven hundredths of a second, but in the races - where the points are paid out - Lawson has a clear advantage.He’s scored in 13 of the 17 grands prix he’s started for Racing Bulls this year, as well as taking points in three of the six sprint races staged. He’s also finished ahead of Lindblad 11 times out of the 14 races they have both finished and run ahead of him on 77% of the racing laps both completed.That’s made him the undisputed king of the midfield. Of the 52 qualifying sessions and races, including sprints, held this year, Lawson has been classified at the top of that group 18 times.To put that number in context, remember Alpine and Audi have made the fight at the front of that group a close one, and that Lawson wasn’t part of the midfield for eight of those because he was in Hadjar’s Red Bull.His approach has also caught the eye. Prior to 2026, there were times when his decision-making in battle could be self-defeating. That led to more on-track incidents than necessary.That’s something he’s largely cut out this year, while still fighting hard enough to get the results.He’s also adapted well to the 2026 cars, recognising he needed to contain the desire to over-drive to get the most out of them - not easy to do for a driver who can be naturally aggressive on corner entries.He’s also able to piece together weekends consistently well, often turning things round even if they start badly on Friday.He also did a good job in those three outings for Red Bull, despite the scars of what happened to him in 2025. That shows a mental robustness, which is also reflected in his mindset amid uncertainty about his future. He’s been able to focus on doing his job and not been distracted by this - something that is easier said than done.Lawson explained: “A year ago I thought about it a lot. It was very much in my head and you just drive worse when you overthink things.”Lawson hasn’t suddenly transformed himself into the best driver in F1. But he’s taken a big step to become a rounded, consistent, and dependable midfield performer - and a very quick one too.That’s what eventually made him undroppable for 2027. Permane had already suggested “everyone will be happy” when the announcement finally came, so that suggests that now Lawson has been confirmed alternative arrangements will be made for Tsolov - which will most likely mean an official reserve driver role and an expanded programme of F1 testing and free practice running in 2027.

item.title: Racing Bulls officially keeps Lawson for 2027
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: Liam Lawson will remain at Racing Bulls next season after the squad announced an unchanged Formula 1 line-up for 2027.The New Zealander’s future had been uncertain for many weeks, with the Red Bull-owned outfit pondering whether to keep him on alongside Arvid Lindblad or promote its junior driver Nikola Tsolov.However, as reported earlier this week, Lawson’s recent strong performances in Mexico and Brazil were understood to have put him on course for a new deal and convinced Racing Bulls he was the best candidate.With Lawson currently sitting ninth in the drivers’ standings, as best of the rest behind the top four teams, and his contribution key to helping Racing Bulls sit fifth in the constructors’ championship, it would have been nonsensical to have dropped him.Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane believed that the line-up of Lawson and Lindblad was the perfect one in terms of blending youth and experience.“Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we’ve seen the progress they’ve made, both individually and as a pairing,” explained Permane.“I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition. Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."Lawson has earned praise in the paddock this year for his standout performances for both Racing Bulls and during a stand-in run at Red Bull, when he filled in for the injured Isack Hadjar.He thanked Racing Bulls for the belief in him.“We've had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I've loved driving,” he said.“It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for P5 in the constructors' championship. "It's a testament to the hard work of everyone both at track, and back at the factory. I’m looking forward to carrying this momentum forward with Arvid through to 2027; we're building something super positive and I’m excited by what we can achieve together.”The Racing Bulls statement that announced Lawson and Lindblad were staying for 2027 did not make any reference to plans for Tsolov, who is in the hunt to clinch the F2 crown this year.The Bulgarian had a rookie FP1 run for Racing Bulls in Mexico, and will likely have a wider role with Red Bull in 2027. He has also been linked with a switch to Super Formula in Japan. item.title: 'No serious damage' – Lucinda Brand escapes serious injury following her crash at the Niel Superprestige
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: After initially fearing the worst, Lucinda Brand was not seriously injured when she hit the barrier during the Superprestige Jaarmarktcross cyclo-cross race at Niel on Wednesday. Early on during round three of the season-long Superprestige series, World Champion Brand briefly lost control of her bike, hitting the barrier and twisting her ankle as she put her foot down.Despite what was apparently an innocuous incident, her discomfort was clear immediately; the 37-year-old first grimaced, then fell into tears, before abandoning the race she had hoped to win for a fifth time.After the incident, her Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions team manager, former World Champion Sven Nys, was fearful Brand had suffered a severe injury, telling Play Sport: "If Lucinda has tears in her eyes, that is usually not a good sign. She is quite a tough cookie, which is why I am a bit worried now."Then, in a post on the team’s Instagram account, he added: "She can’t put force on her foot right now, so I think it’s important that we monitor that and make sure that nothing was damaged. "Hoping we won’t lose her for the rest of the season."However, Nys has since been reassured. "Everything is okay. No serious damage was detected; she just needs to make sure it doesn’t happen again. Taping the foot is important now, though," he told Belgian paper .The season continues apace this weekend, and Brand would have been expected to start round four of the Superprestige at Merkplas on Saturday and Sunday’s Bollekesccross, the second round of the X2O Badkamers Trofee, a series she leads, after winning the Koppenbergcross, and which she has won on four previous occasions. However, following her injury, Brand’s participation is yet to be confirmed.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: 'I don't get often very emotional' – Tadej Pogačar highlights a teammate's Tour de France stage win as 'one of the best days of my career'
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: Tadej Pogačar has no shortage of highlights from his eight years so far as a professional bike racer but he has picked out a teammate’s victory as "one of the best days of my career"."The first stages, nine, was really nice," Pogačar says from a massage table, presumably after stage nine as he talks about it being “super hot” and references "three victories" taken by the team. "I think the one that Isaac wins, in Barcelona, I got also really emotional, and I don’t get often very emotional," Pogačar says."So, one of the best days of my career," he adds. The comments are brief but striking in the context of all that Pogačar has won, including five Tour de France titles, 26 Tour de France stages of his own, 13 Monument Classics, and two world titles. For all the talk of his insatiable appetite for victory, he seemingly took just as much joy in sacrificing the chance of another one and helping someone else, who may one day come to rival him. And it wasn’t just that day in Barcelona; with a commanding lead in the yellow jersey Pogačar went on to effectively work as a domestique for Del Toro again and again in the second half of the Tour de France, notably on the stage 15 summit finish at Plateau de Solaison and on the penultimate day to Alpe d’Huez when Del Toro’s podium position came under fire from Paul Seixas. "You try to be the best version of yourself but we don’t know how we are perceived in the third person," Del Toro said in a recent interview with Spanish newspaper in reference to Pogačar’s treatment of him."That he can see something that maybe I’m not seeing is flattering, but also quite something. He wants to be part of my process and support me in each opportunity. It’s something very beautiful and I feel very privileged."'POG1 – The Making of a Legend', made by Colnago Cultura, premieres on Friday November 13 at 3pm GMT / 10am ET on Colnago's YouTube channel, where it will be available to watch worldwide for free.

item.title: Russell launches fully-funded new karting academy
item.author: Fleur Mealing
item.content:encoded: Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has launched a new karting academy at Silverstone aimed at developing the next generation of motorsport talent, with 25 young drivers set to receive a fully funded championship opportunity in 2027.The GR63 Karting Academy will be open to boys and girls aged eight and nine, with Russell hoping to provide a route into motorsport for talented youngsters who might otherwise be held back by the financial demands of the sport.Based at Silverstone's karting circuit, the initiative will run across four stages, beginning with open-access qualifying sessions in December 2026.The first stage will see eligible drivers compete in arrive-and-drive sessions between December 6 and 31, with the 80 fastest progressing to a shootout on January 31, 2027.From there, 25 drivers will be selected for the GR63 Championship, an eight-round series running from March to November 2027. Each round will take place on a different circuit configuration at Silverstone, with all participation costs covered by the academy.The 25 selected drivers will also receive a full set of academy equipment, including racing overalls, a helmet, gloves and boots.The programme will culminate in December 2027, when the championship's top five finishers compete in a final race at Silverstone. Drivers will be evaluated on their talent, lap times, fitness, racecraft and media skills, with the overall winner receiving a fully-funded karting season in 2028.Russell will help mentor and guide participants throughout the programme."Karting is where it all started for me, and it taught me everything I've relied on throughout my career," said Russell."I know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight."With the GR63 Karting Academy, I want to give something back by finding those hidden talents and giving them the support and platform they need to reach their potential."The financial accessibility of the programme is a central part of its appeal. While the initial qualifying sessions will cost £25 and entry to the January shootout will cost £75, everything from the championship stage onwards will be fully funded.The initiative is being supported by Silverstone and the British Racing Drivers' Club (BRDC), with BRDC president David Coulthard welcoming the opportunity to invest in Britain's motorsport future."The GR63 Academy captures that ethos perfectly, and we are delighted to work with George to support the next generation of drivers here at Silverstone," said Coulthard.How to enter the GR63 Karting AcademyThe initial arrive-and-drive qualifying sessions will take place at Silverstone Kart Track between December 6 and 31, 2026, at a cost of £25.All applicants must be citizens of a Commonwealth country.

item.title: Why Mercedes cannot dominate F1's new era
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: They say history doesn't repeat itself, but it often rhymes. And that applies to Formula 1 as well.The start of new-rules eras have often been hugely indicative of what is to come, as the trends of the inaugural season lay down the story of future years.If we do some comparisons of the first years of the most recent major rules-change eras, we can see how the comparisons between the first and second half of each of those seasons gave us a hint of what was to come in the following campaigns.Constructors' championship splitsRepresented as first half / second half / total: 112 / 60 / 172: 92.5 / 61.0 / 153.5: 14 / 57 / 71: 32 / 38 / 70: 34.5 / 25 / 59.5: 366 / 335 / 701: 188 / 217 / 405: 121 / 199 / 320: 116 / 100 / 216: 96 / 85 / 1812022 (22 rounds; 11 / 11): 359 / 400 / 759: 303 / 251 / 554: 237 / 278 / 515: 81 / 92 / 173: 81 / 78 / 1592026 (23 rounds; 20 completed so far; 11 / 9): 379 / 273 / 652: 307 / 203 / 510: 177 / 238 / 415: 222 / 176 / 398In 2009, Brawn GP took the crowns thanks to its stellar start to the year, but you could see Red Bull getting its act together ahead of what became its era of dominance.In 2014, Mercedes was unstoppable and its advantage through the year clearly told us about it becoming the main force in F1.In 2022, Ferrari started well but Red Bull got the weight off its car and pushed forward to begin Max Verstappen's real run of supremacy, off the back of his maiden title the year before.For 2026, Mercedes has secured both crowns, but the story of the year is an intriguing one because a trend has emerged of there being no clear benchmark late on.While Kimi Antonelli and George Russell kicked 2026 off strongly and laid title-winning foundations early on, subsequent spells of success for Red Bull, McLaren and Ferrari have pointed to a shift.In fact, as the table below shows, if you take the results of the last five races up until and including Brazil, Mercedes is only the third-highest-scoring team.Top four constructors (last five rounds)Last five total points: 152Overall total: 415 (3rd0Last five total points: 132Overall total: 510 (2nd)Last five total points: 114Overall total: 652 (1st)Last five total points: 92Overall total: 398 (4tth)F1 has a super-close top four where no team seems to have been able to edge clear of its rivals, and it has been hard to pick out anyone who has built up some momentum.This is why, for all the joy that Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has taken from getting his team back to title-winning ways, he has no sense that this is the start of "runaway" success."It looks like the most competitive era that is about to start," he said."The teams have become so professional in capability and resource that these kind of runaway seasons, I don't see them anymore, whether it's four in a row or eight in a row. And that is a completely new challenge."You can see how quickly it goes from you being dominant and within a few races you realise that your upgrade doesn't work and you fall back and you're just third on the road. So it's great for the sport."I wish it was the era of Mercedes and me running away with another few championships. I don't think it's the reality."The upgrade war seems to have had the effect of repeatedly shuffling the order of the top four.Whenever any of the major teams have brought big development steps, often those have helped push them to the front and changed the hierarchy.McLaren team principal Andrea Stella has labelled this "ping pong season" in terms of how teams bounce between being at the front or the back of that top-four block."Anybody that upgrades kind of takes an advantage, but even if you do a good job of developing, not necessarily [is it the case that] you can establish yourself at the top," he said recently."We have a variable level of supremacy, dependent on the track conditions or the optimisation of the set-up."But the reality is that I think nowhere before we have had F1 so competitive and with such a rate of development. If we raced with the race-one car [from the Australia season opener], we will be one and a half seconds slower than what we are at the moment."The cause of this major shuffling is not only the fact that the big teams all seem to be so evenly matched in terms of their capability. (And have found ways to all keep pushing on with developments under the cost cap.)It is that the FIA appears to have made life very difficult for teams because the aero regulations are so restrictive, leaving designers with only very small areas they can work on.Focused on creating cars that did not produce significant dirty air, the FIA was determined not to allow areas that teams could exploit to ruin this and improve downforce.And this has left teams capped in terms of how much performance they have been able to eke out.Stella added: "If you take the regulations and you define the volumes within which you can put aerodynamic devices, that's not how an aerodynamicist would do it."They [the rules] have been done in a certain way somehow to jeopardise for the sake of competition and also for the sake of allowing the following and the overtaking."Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies agreed on the lack of design freedom leading to diminishing returns for all teams."The convergence is probably happening earlier than what we all thought," he said. "I'm guessing somehow, it's perhaps an indication of fairly restrictive regulations."That being said, you see cars with visibly different concepts and you see four top teams fighting, which is probably a great point to be for the sport."So, let's see how it will pan out in the second year. But to be already in the second part of '26 in situations where you turn up at the race weekend and you don't know which one of the four top teams is going to win the race, I think it's great for the sport."The end result of all this is a form book that is in a state of flux.Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur thought that the 'ping pong' element of rapidly shuffling fortunes was a consequence of immature rules offering potential for big gains, something that will slow down into next season where he felt teams would converge more."Each time that we were bringing something, we are doing a step," he said. "That was a little bit the story of the season because, as we [the top-four teams] were not bringing upgrades at the same races, you have this kind of rotation."Probably it could be less through next year and the following years, but we will have a kind of convergence of performance of where we are next year."And it's for this reason that Wolff was convinced that it is important Mercedes gets back to its early performance levels now that give it a springboard into next year."Look at the last few races: we haven't won [Mercedes has one win in the last five]," he said in Brazil."The competition has been getting tougher, between Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull and ourselves. It's four teams that can win races and will be challenging for a world championship. And I have no doubt that it's going to be very difficult for us next year."For me, the 2027 season has started now."

item.title: Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair
item.author: Hettie O'Brien
item.content:encoded: In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen HuangGood morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies.Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines.| Ministers are considering changing the law to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand.| The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.| Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states.| Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years, setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power.| Police officers risk arresting innocent people, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can’t be at the bottom indefinitely’: Can Britain’s most maligned service station be turned around?
item.author: Imogen West-Knights
item.content:encoded: In 2022 and 2023, Hartshead Moor East, near Leeds, was voted the worst in Great Britain. Ever since, staff have been on a mission to redeem its reputationThe crime issue of the Long Read magazine is out now. Click here to orderIn October 2023, at Skelton Lake service station on the M1 south-east of Leeds, Janine Gray received some bad news. She was surrounded by journalists and leading lights from the transport industry: people from the AA, the RAC, motorway service area chief executives, officials from National Highways. The big dogs. And it was among these gathered dignitaries that Gray heard the news she had been hoping, for the previous 12 months, not to hear. For the second year running, Hartshead Moor East – one half of the motorway services near Leeds that she managed – had been officially declared the worst service station in Britain.This poll, conducted annually by the consumer watchdog Transport Focus, always makes the news. It produces gags on Have I Got News For You, punning headlines in the papers, “and finally” segments on local TV channels. Now Gray and her staff would be subjected to another round of ridicule. Of all the country’s service stations, which have a sort of aura of shitness to them anyway, theirs was apparently the shittest. Again.Continue reading...

item.title: Cavaliers 115, Knicks 107: Scenes from a wide free throw gap
item.author: Russell Richardson
item.content:encoded: Four nights ago, in Cleveland, the Knicks beat the Cavaliers by 12 points thanks to dominant second and third quarters. Tonight, as we saluted our veterans, the two teams squared up once more, this time at Madison Square Garden. Yet again, our heroes dropped the first frame, but won the second, tied the third, and managed to tie the game midway through the fourth. The Cavs were determined not to let this one slip through their fingers, and with season-highs for two of ’em, James Harden (32 PTS, 9-14 FG) and Tyrese Proctor (15 PTS), they sealed the win in the final minutes, 115-107.With his eleventh double-double, Karl-Anthony Towns (21 PTS, 11 RBS, 7-11 FG) tied Willis Reed for the longest double-double streak to start a Knicks season. They shot better from the floor and in the paint, but the guests attempted 14 more free throws. It didn’t help that New York surrendered 19 points off turnovers.Last week, Peyton Watson (7 PTS) took most of Cleveland’s shots to start the game. This time, Kenny Atkinson’s club leveled its attack. Their defense hummed, too, with Evan Mobley (10 PTS, 5 RBS) and Watson swatting down shots, and Donovan Mitchell (23 PTS) and Harden picking pockets. Benchman Proctor led the team with eight points in the quarter, while Watson crashed the boards and spread out dimes. Jarrett Allen, who missed last week’s contest, cleared five early boards and finished with an 11-14 double-double.Josh Hart (6 PTS, 26 MIN), back in the lineup after missing three games (ankle, illness), surely had nothing to do with the Knicks’ starters dragging their heels. Jalen Brunson (27 PTS, 12-23 FG) and OG Anunoby (14 PTS) were the only Knicks with points until Mohamed Diawara checked in midway through the frame and scored. Mitchell picked on the sophomore, dribbled around him, and burned him with a fadeaway.The hometown club converted 25% of its first eight longball tries and attempted no free throws in the first frame. Strange but true. Towns, Brunson, and Shamet had the hot hands early, while Mikal Bridges, Josh Hart, and Andre Drummond combined to shoot 0-for-6 in the first half. Bridges would usually defend Mitchell, but Brown assigned Shamet to him. You can feel the coach’s confidence waning, no? The Ohio Players hit nine straight shots, led by as many as 12, and won the quarter, 33–23.We weren’t sweating the first quarter. New York dropped the first period by one in their previous matchup. Tonight, they opened the second on a 9–1 run behind Towns, Shamet, and Tyler Kolek. The latter hit two buckets and was a team-high plus-eight as the good guys climbed back into the game. Towns was cooking, too, scoring 13 points in his first 13 minutes, grabbing seven boards, and stuffing Allen’s shot. Miles McBride hit three threes in under two minutes, including the one that erased the last of a 12-point deficit and knotted the game at 43.Brunson splashed a go-ahead three, but Harden answered with two of his own, Mitchell hit his freebies, and Mobley dunked to push Cleveland’s lead back to six. Mike Brown tried to give Towns a breather and watched the Knicks’ progress evaporate without him. KAT jumped back in and dunked with authority.During the period, Brunson reached 11,000 career points, 3,000 assists, and 1,000 three-pointers. He’s one of seven active players in that club, along with LeBron James, Harden, Damian Lillard, Devin Booker, Luka Dončić, and Trae Young. Congratulations, Cap!At halftime, the guests were ahead 59–53. Harden led all scorers with 17 (5-of-7 FG), while KAT topped the Knicks with 15. Bizarrely, New York took a single free throw all half, and Cleveland’s seven extra points at the line more than covered the margin. Both teams made 22 field goals (52% for Cleveland, 51% for New York) and grabbed 17 boards apiece. Cleveland had a 26–20 edge in the paint, but New York shot 40% from three to the Cavs’ 37% and scored one more point from the field.Cleveland opened the third on a 10–5 run, with threes from Watson, Mitchell, and Harden stretching the lead to 69–58. Spida missed his next two threes and picked up a charge. From there, the hosts got serious. Brunson scored five of his eight points in the stretch during an 11–0 run that tied the tilt at 69, while the visitors blanked on eight consecutive attempts. Towns helped fuel the run by setting up Brunson and Shamet for buckets and blocking Watson at the cup. Hart later found McBride for another tying three at 74. Cleveland closed the quarter on an 8–2 run to take an 82–76 advantage into Q4.Rough stretch for Bridges. He sat at the eight-minute mark of the third and came back with under two minutes left in the quarter. Allen blocked him on a layup, then took the ball away. Somehow, New York had attempted just five free throws through 40 minutes, all by Towns. The Cavs had taken 19 by then, eight by Harden alone.Deuce scored the first five points of the fourth to pull the Knicks within one, but Mitchell answered with two layups, the second an and-one, and Proctor capped a 7–0 Cleveland run. Spida had two turnovers that led to McBride baskets, but he also set up Maleek Thomas for two buckets. With Brunson on the bench, McBride and Kolek ran the backcourt. Kolek fed Shamet for a three and KAT for a dunk that cut the deficit to seven with 7:35 left. Anunoby went on a tear with two freebies, a longball, a steal, and a breakaway feed to Hart for a bunny. Tie score at 99 with 5:36 to go.Out of a timeout, Harden, Mobley, and Brunson scored to make it 106–103 with 2:18 on the clock. The game was still within reach, but Drummond fouled Mitchell and Allen scored four straight points, capitalizing on Brunson’s long brick. The deficit reached five with a minute to go. Brunson missed on a contested drive, Watson blocked McBride from behind on the fast break, and Harden hit his free throws. Ball game.A Cup game in Indiana on Friday. Mo is tightening the bolts on his recap. Safe travels, Knickerbockers.

item.title: Classic British steel bike maker Temple Cycles set to close after 12 years in business
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Bristol-based bike maker Temple Cycles is set to close after more than 12 years in business, with its two shops also shutting down.The company specialises in manufacturing steel-framed bikes, selling them either online or from its Bristol- and London-based shops, but will close down, with all its premises already listed as closed online. However, the company’s website and social media accounts are still live, and though most models are listed as sold out, orders for frame sets, parts and accessories are invited in a Facebook post as recently as Tuesday, November 10. That was the same day local news site, Bristol 24/7, reported that the company’s owner, Matt Mears, had emailed investors that their money would not be returned and the business would be winding down.The closure follows two crowdfunding campaigns, first in 2017 and again in 2022."You put your money and trust into Temple, and I’m very sorry that the business hasn’t delivered the outcome we hoped for. I know this is disappointing news," Mears wrote, according to Bristol 24/7.In the email, Mears explained the company had experienced issues with their supply chain along with rising costs for materials and energy, saying: "It’s an exceptionally difficult time to run a bicycle business.""We’ve worked hard to turn the business around while managing persistent pressure on cash flow. We substantially reduced overheads, launched new products, relocated our headquarters and opened a new showroom."Our electric bike performed well, but this was offset by weaker sales elsewhere."The business also has existing debt commitments, and I don’t see a realistic route to generating the profits and cash reserves needed to meet them. Taken together, I no longer believe the current model offers a realistic route to a sustainable business," Mears said in his email. Bristol 24/7 also reports that Mears hopes to continue in the bicycle industry, using his experience in another business focussed on parts and accessories. Mears launched Temple in 2014 while still an engineering student at Bristol University, the business making a variety of steel-framed bikes, mostly using tubes from compatriot company, Birmingham-based Reynolds. Their range includes regular road bikes, gravel, hybrid and city bikes, alongside E-bikes and even step-through frames. As recently as April 2026, Temple opened a new workshop and retail on the outskirts of Bristol.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Even post-Mitchell Robinson, the Knicks are feasting on the glass
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: When the Knicks lost Mitchell Robinson in the offseason, there was not only a sense of mourning for losing the services of the longest-tenured Knick right after a championship, but also in the sense of what he provided on the court.Even with his injury-prone nature, Robinson was a premier rim protector and an anchor for the Knicks’ defense whenever he was on the court, which would be enough of an asset on his own, but the biggest asset he provided was something entirely different.As we all came to know and love, he is simply the best offensive rebounder of this generation and one of the best rebounders, period, in the NBA. His innate ability to gobble up boards helped turbocharge an offense that already had plenty of offensive weapons, but would sometimes struggle with inefficiency.For several years now, the Knicks have built their offense around the expectation of extra possessions. They’ve game-planned to win games by simply getting more opportunities to score than their opponents by grabbing more rebounds and committing fewer turnovers. With Robinson gone, the former was in serious danger, even if the team signed Andre Drummond to bandage it. Through 10 games this season, though, they seem to have not missed a beat. The Knicks are impressively the No. 1 rebounding team in basketball so far. That’s powered by Drummond not missing a beat with his usual rebounding prowess, but also an elevation in the team’s process and scheme.Karl-Anthony Towns, historically a great rebounding center, leads the NBA with a staggering 13.8 rebounds per game. While his defensive strides have been the most encouraging part of the start of this season, he’s been a huge part of winning the possession battle by hitting another level with a 36.6 DREB%, which also leads the league.As a team, the Knicks have hauled in 55.5 percent of available rebounds, 73 percent of defensive rebounds, and 38.8 percent of offensive rebounds, all leading the NBA. They’ve done this despite routinely having smaller lineups on the court.Over the last two years, the Knicks were an elite rebounding team, especially thanks to double-big lineups and versatility. They’ve gradually gotten smaller as a team, have played zero minutes with more than one player taller than 6’8” on the court, and are still dominating on the glass.Towns, Drummond, and Josh Hart have combined to do a bulk of the rebounding on both ends, but it’s also been a group effort. OG Anunoby has been much more active on the glass, averaging 1.7 OREB/g. Mikal Bridges and Jordan Clarkson are grabbing more rebounds on a rate basis. Even Jalen Brunson is averaging a career high in offensive rebounds.Everyone is feeding off each other. Of the Knicks’ 10 most-used lineups, nine of them have an elite rebounding percentage, with the lone exception being a shocker: the starting five (47.5%). Their early-season struggles, particularly on offense, are worth monitoring, but some positive regression is due whenever Hart returns from his ankle/illness ailments, especially in the rebounding department. The team as a whole played poorly through five games and has only started to pick it up recently.The synergy has allowed them to just take the soul out of teams in recent games, something that’s been pivotal to their success in recent years. Just look at last night’s game against Milwaukee, where, despite the plucky Bucks chopping a 26-point lead down to 11, they couldn’t overcome a 59-32 rebounding disadvantage.Against Cleveland on Saturday, the Knicks took advantage of no Jarrett Allen to outrebound the Cavs, 49-40, to help stretch their second-half cushion. In the blowout of the Bulls last week, it was another 57-34 bludgeoning.It even makes you think: was it the system that made Mitchell Robinson who he was, or was he just a superpowered cog in the wheel?Let’s slow down. Robinson was always a generational rebounder, as evidenced by his work under previous head coaches, but his early struggles in Boston are notable.As long as Towns continues to be consistent defensively and the team keeps rebounding like this… will they even miss him that much?

item.title: 'If she has tears in her eyes, that is not a good sign' – Fears for Lucinda Brand's cyclo-cross season as world champion injures ankle in opening-lap crash
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Cyclo-cross World Champion Lucinda Brand season could be in doubt, after she was forced out of the Superprestige race at Niel in tears following an opening-lap crash that left her in tears.Brand arrived for the Jaarmarktcross hoping to take her fifth win in the event, which formed the third round of the season-long Superprestige series, but the most innocuous of crashes left her barely able to walk.She started the race on the back foot, trying to make up time on Amandine Fouquenet (Pauwels Sauzen-Altez Industriebouw), who had blazed her way through the sand pit to build an early lead. However, as Brand set off in pursuit in the muddy conditions, she was pushed into the barrier on a small climb, apparently twisting her ankle as her foot hit the ground.While she carried on for a few seconds, riding through the pit area, she then abandoned and was barely able to stand as she dismounted. Though she was seen riding off, her Baloise-Poetsbureau team manager Sven Nys has cast doubt on the rest of her season."Lucinda twisted her ankle in the first round, where she made a misstep," Nys said in a statement from the team. "She lost her line, she can’t put force on her foot right now, so I think it’s important that we monitor that and make sure that nothing was damaged. Hoping we won’t lose her for the rest of the season."Nys also spoke with the host broadcaster Play Sports immediately after the race, saying: "She told me that she went off the track and wanted to put her foot down, but she twisted it, she couldn't put any weight on it anymore. I told her she needs to have everything checked to make sure no ligaments were damaged," Sporza reported him as saying. "But if Lucinda has tears in her eyes, that is usually not a good sign. She is quite a tough cookie, which is why I am a bit worried now."Brand has been the dominant force in cyclo-cross in recent seasons, winning the rainbow jersey twice, the World Cup and X2O Badkamers Trofee four times and the Superprestige on three occasions, as well as taking a total of 89 career wins.At the weekend, she won her second European title after Luxembourgish rider Marie Schreiber was relegated for an irregular sprint.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Game Preview: Knicks vs. Cavaliers, November 11, 2026
item.author: Kento Kato
item.content:encoded: Remember when the Knicks started 0-3, and people thought that the sky was falling? Turns out talks of the team no longer being good were exaggerated after all.New York has now won six of their last seven games and are now winners of four straight after Tuesday night’s thrashing of a Bucks team that has been maybe even worse than expected. Part of that can and should be attributed to a lighter schedule over the last couple of weeks. The Knicks have played the 1-8 Bulls twice, the 2-8 Nets, and the aforementioned 1-10 Bucks. Of their two quality wins during that stretch, one was against the 7-3 Pistons and the other came against the Cavaliers, the latter perhaps not that great a deal given the interesting season they’ve had and the fact they were playing on the end of a back-to-back.Up until the Bulls game last week, I would’ve called the Knicks’ season a roller coaster ride. But whatever early-season turbulence and disappointments the Knicks experienced, the Cavaliers might have surpassed it. At 5-6, they are just 1.5 games behind the Knicks. And it’s only been 11 games. But the Cavaliers have lost two in a row, have lost four of five and five of seven.A lot of it starts with the starting lineup, which is ironic given the ceaseless talks surrounding the Knicks’ very own starters. Coming into Wednesday night, the Cavaliers’ preferred starting lineup of James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen has an abysmal net rating of -18.9 in 84 minutes together. That number is a lot better when one of Mobley, Watson, or Allen is off the court, with the net ratings in those minutes all being positive, suggesting that the talent is there, but the synergy may not be.There are three players in particular who deserve a closer look. Harden is currently averaging 15.3PPG and 5.7APG both of which are the third and fourth lowest of his career, respectively. He’s currently shooting just 35.5% from three, 37.5% from two, and shooting just 4.8FTA/G. Given how little he provides as a defender, he’s been a tough watch this season, and the numbers back it up. In the 359 minutes with Harden on the floor, the Cavaliers have had a -6.0 net rating. In the 174 minutes with him off the floor, they have a +16.5 net rating. That’s a 22.5-point swing.He isn’t the only one that has been a disappointment, though. Watson, the Cavaliers’ major off-season trade acquisition, was looked to be the athletic shooting wing with size that could finally lock down the small forward position. Critics of the move were cautious given how much he benefitted from Nikola Jokic’s gravity and passing, but also given his relatively small sample size of being the kind of player the Cavaliers were hoping to get. While it’s unfair to judge Watson on just nine games in a new city and situation, he’s been a subpar player. Watson is currently averaging just 11.4PPG and 4.6RPG while having an assist-to-turnover ratio of 2.7:1.8 and is shooting a putrid 21.6% from three and barely hovering above 40% from the field. And like Harden, he’s been a negative when on the floor. The Cavaliers have a -5.2 net rating in the 250 minutes with him on the floor. Some of that may simply be due to the fact that he has to share a large chunk of his minutes with Harden. But it also doesn’t fully explain why the Cavaliers have a +7.1 net rating in the 283 minutes without him or why the starting lineup sans Watson actually has a +30.4 net rating in 23 minutes.Maybe the most interesting case study, though, is Mobley. His individual stats look fine for the most part. He’s averaging 17.5PPG and 7.5RPG while shooting 55.8% from the field and 50% from three. But the Cavaliers are a -2.4 in his minutes. And even when he shares the floor with Mitchell and Allen, the trio is a -20.5 in 87 minutes. Meanwhile, the duo of Mitchell and Allen without Mobley is a whopping +26.1 in 67 minutes with Mitchell being a +7.0 in his minutes and Allen being a +5.0 in his.The team can still turn things around. As Knicks fans were told to do after 144 regular season minutes, Cavaliers fans should be reminded to relax because it really is a marathon. But as you can see, there are some very clear holes in this team. Some have pointed to Kenny Atkinson’s inability to fully get this group to gel. I do think there is some validity to that. He’s either not making the requisite changes or his players aren’t listening. And either can be a fireable offense. But he can’t bear all of the blame.The team has very little depth. And at the end of the day, it comes down to his players simply playing better. Harden can’t shoot this bad if he’s going to give close to zero effort defensively. Watson needs to shoot better. And Mobley, despite putting together a solid campaign statistically, needs to continue becoming much more of an aggressive force both offensively and defensively. All that being said, the Knicks are in prime position to extend their winning streak to five. They took care of business against the lowly Bucks last night, which allowed their starters to rest. Not a single player played more than 29 minutes, so they should be ready tonight. It can be difficult to beat a team twice in such a short span, but given the Cavaliers’ recent struggles and how well the Knicks have played them as of late, New York should be favored.When you play a team with expectations, such as the Cavaliers, that has underperformed the way they have, you run the risk of running into a hungry and sometimes even angry team. Cleveland has the talent on paper to beat anybody on any given night. But we saw last Saturday that this team doesn’t have a single player that can defend Jalen Brunson or Karl-Anthony Towns, and they just do not have the depth, especially at the center position, to reliably stay physical with a team like the Knicks. With New York finally finding their groove and Cleveland slipping, I expect a closer game than the last one, but the Knicks to hold them off, improving to 7-4.Who: New York Knicks (6-4) vs. Cleveland Cavaliers (5-6)Date: Wednesday, November 11, 2026Place: Madison Square Garden, New York, NYFollow: @ptknicksblog and bsky

item.title: Hamilton loses 'most marketable athlete' status in 2026
item.author: Samarth Kanal
item.content:encoded: Lewis Hamilton is no longer sport’s most marketable athlete - or even the most marketable Formula 1 driver, having fallen behind Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc - in the latest rankings created by media and events business SportsPro.Hamilton was top of the 2025 SportsPro marketability rankings for athletes, with a total marketability score of 96.03 out of 100.In 2026, Hamilton is ranked 22nd. His marketability score is 66.63, on par with footballers Neymar and Vinicius Junior.Hamilton’s team-mate Leclerc is ahead in ninth on the list with a marketability score of 71.12, up from 25th in the 2025 list with a score of 75.03. The next-highest driver is Max Verstappen (48th, up from 81st last year), while 2025 champion Lando Norris (78th) is now ranked behind McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri (56th) having been 23 places ahead in 41st last year.New champion Kimi Antonelli is the lowest placed F1 driver who made the top 150 in 126th, a 48-place drop from 78th in 2025.MotoGP rider Marc Marquez is the only motorsport athlete not tied to F1 on the list, ranking 86th, five places above Alpine F1 driver Pierre Gasly.Belarusian tennis player Aryna Sabalenka is top of the list with, ahead of Chinese skier Eileen Gu, Greek basketball player Giannis Antetokounmpo, Norwegian footballer Erling Haaland, and Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz.American athletes make up 32% of the top 150 while British and Indian athletes are next with 7.3% of the pie apiece.Football (soccer) has 33 athletes on the list and a 22% share of the list while motorsport’s eight representatives (5.3%) put it sixth on the list of sports, behind tennis and cricket but ahead of golf and boxing. Female NASCAR driver Toni Breidinger and F1 driver Liam Lawson dropped off the list having appeared in 2025.How the marketability scores are calculated - why is Hamilton lower than Leclerc?The marketability score is a combination of brand equity, momentum, and commercial trajectory, three metrics that are calculated by combining "several hundred data points" and more than 3000 brand partnership records over July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026.Scroll down to see how the motorsport athletes rank within the top 150.Brand equity is the strength and trust of the athlete’s brand, momentum is the rate at which the athlete’s value is growing, and commercial trajectory is the room for an athlete’s future commercial growth. The latter metric is given the smallest weighting out of the three, and the scores are relative rather than absolute; Sabalenka’s ranking puts her top with the other athletes in mind. Leclerc, 29, has a higher brand equity score than Hamilton but a lower momentum score. The Monegasque’s ranking of commercial trajectory also boosts his ranking compared to Hamilton.Age and longevity in the sport has an impact on the trajectory score: at 41 Hamilton is the joint-oldest athlete on the list with Cristiano Ronaldo and LeBron James.Furthermore, Leclerc scores highly on the commercial trajectory metric, implying that there is strength in his brand that hasn’t been converted into commercial returns compared to Hamilton.Leclerc scores high in brand equity due to his personal style and public presentation, plus the size of his audience and how actively that audience engages with his brand. Chris Collins, president of NorthStar (which powers the rankings) said to BlackBook Motorsport that Leclerc has "one of the strongest established brands of any athlete in the world."He ranks second of all 247 athletes we assessed on brand equity, built on how he presents himself, a compelling personal story and premium partners who keep choosing to work with him."As one of the most-followed drivers on the grid, it’s little surprise to see his audience scores performing well, but it also emphasises that his followers actively interact with his profile. He also benefits from a high audience breadth score, an expected outcome for all Formula 1 drivers thanks to their global profile."He added of Hamilton: "What keeps him below the top 10 isn’t his brand, it’s time. At 41, there is naturally less career runway ahead, and a forward-looking assessment should read a great career in its later chapters exactly that way."

item.title: Superprestige Niel: Cameron Mason soloes to first win of the season and biggest victory of his career
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Cameron Mason (777TV) soloed to the biggest win of his career in the third round of the 2026-27 Superprestige, the Jaarmarktcross in Niel. The British champion got the better of Joran Wyseure (Crelan-Corendon) in a two-man battle over the final laps of the race.The pair were the last men standing from a four-rider leading group after both Kevin Kuhn (Heizomat-Cube) and Michael Vanthourenhout (Pauwels Sauzen-Atlez Industriebouw) dropped away due to a puncture and a fall earlier on.In the end, Mason carried a small gap into the closing eighth lap and pulled out a winning advantage in the sandpit before carrying a 20-second lead to the line to celebrate victory.Joris Nieuwenhuis (Heizomat-Cube) grabbed the final podium spot, having been chasing the leaders alone since lap five. The Dutchman ended the race 27 seconds down on Mason and 12 seconds up on fourth-placed Felipe Orts (Euskaltel-Euskadi).Mason now leads the Superprestige overall rankings, his 15-point haul taking him to 39 in three races, one better than Wyseure. Vanthourenhout is third overall on 37 points, having picked up just eight points here after finishing down in eighth place.It was Kuhn who led from the start, with Vanthourenhout and Kuhn's teammate Nieuwenhuis getting separation from the rest to lead the chase. Further back, Wyseure and Niels Vendeputte were the best of the rest but over 10 seconds down.Vanthourenhout left Nieuwenhuis behind on lap two to get across to Kuhn. Cameron Mason made it three up front on lap three, while Nieuwenhuis and Wyseure also came back as Kuhn continued to lead.On lap four, Vanthourenhout took the lead, a second up on Kuhn, with the other three all within five seconds of him. Up front, the Belgian was beginning to pull away, however. Kuhn, Mason, and Nieuwenhuis dropped away, leaving Wyseure as the main chaser behind the leader, eight seconds back at the start of the fifth lap.Vanthourenhout's spell out front wouldn't last long as Wyseure, Kuhn, and Mason all came back partway through the lap. The quartet were inseparable heading into lap six as Nieuwenhuis chased alone at 11 seconds down.Kuhn, suffering a possible front puncture, was the first to drop from the lead group, losing contact with the front of the race and dropping back to Nieuwenhuis.Wyseure took over the top spot heading into the latter part of the lap, though Vanthourenhout and Mason stuck with him into lap seven, the penultimate lap of the race. A Wyseure bike change to start the lap left him with a few seconds to make up, but he quickly came back to once again make it three up front.Drama struck midway through the lap as Vanthourenhout fell while carrying his bike through a section of deep mud. He lost all momentum in pursuit of his fifth win of the season as a result, losing 20 seconds and dropping out of contention.Up front, Mason and Wyseure continued in the lead with Nieuwenhuis chasing 10 seconds back. Mason had the advantage, though, leading the way and then pulling out a gap late in the lap to start the final lap four seconds up on Wyseure.Mason's ability to ride through the sandpit made all the difference on the final lap, with Wyseure having to dismount in the chase. That meant Mason pulled out a 13-second gap and some breathing space heading into the latter part of the lap. Mason kept pushing and made no mistakes through the mid-section of the lap, pulling out a 20-second gap to Wyseure, who was now only a handful of seconds up on Nieuwenhuis.The Superprestige competition continues with round four on Sunday, November 11, at the Aardbiencross in Merksplace.Cameron Mason (GBr) 777TV CX TeamJoran Wyseure (Bel) Crelan-CorendonJoris Nieuwenhuis (Ned) Heizomat-CubeFelipe Orts Lloret (Spa) Euskaltel-EuskadiGiel Lejeune (Bel) Alpecin-Premier TechKevin Kuhn (Swi) Heizomat-CubeRyan Kamp (Ned) Team Bomba JoinMichael Vanthourenhout (Bel) Pauwels Sauzen-Altez IndustriebouwJente Michels (Bel) Alpecin-Premier TechMees Hendrikx (Ned) Team Bomba JoinNiels Vandeputte (Bel) Alpecin-Premier TechViktor Vandenberghe (Bel) Pauwels Sauzen-Altez IndustriebouwThomas Mein (GBr) Hope Factory RacingVictor Van De Putte (Bel) Charles Liégois CX TeamToon Vandebosch (Bel) Crelan-CorendonKay De Bruyckere (Bel) Pauwels Sauzen-Altez IndustriebouwLorenzo Marasco (Fra) Sebmotobikes CX TeamLukas Herrmann (Ger) Heizomat-CubeDeclan Oldham (GBr) Hope Factory RacingMartynas Medelinskas (Ltu)Raphaël Kockelmann (Lux) Sebmotobikes CX TeamLaurens Sweeck (Bel) Crelan-CorendonThe road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down.
